course_aims: This course aims to provide graduate students with the professional communication skills, anatomical knowledge base, and related assessment skills necessary for clinical practice as an occupational therapist.

learning_outcomes.description: Understand Professional Roles and Reflective Practice . Describe the role of occupational therapists in contemporary practice across various contexts and engage in self-reflection and reflective practice to identify personal values, beliefs, and interpersonal characteristics that influence professional practice.

Develop Communication and Therapeutic Skills. Demonstrate foundational therapeutic communication skills necessary for professional communication, including interviewing, therapeutic use of self, and the ability to adapt and critique communication approaches to support client needs/client engagement and occupational performance.
Demonstrate knowledge of methods in assessing components of neurological function (such as sensory evaluation, tone, and coordination).
Apply theoretical knowledge of human anatomy to identify and palpate anatomical structures on the living body and perform range of motion (ROM) measurement and manual muscle testing (MMT).
Demonstrate effective communication skills when handling and assessing individuals.
Demonstrate professional skills including the ability to evaluate learning and performance of self and others and to work collaboratively within a team.

assessment_details.task_description: This practical viva exam assesses a core skill in occupational therapy, and students must achieve a passing grade of 5 or above (> 65%) to pass the assessment item. Students will be asked to perform one range-of-motion and one manual muscle test on a peer. Students will receive an automatic fail on that test if they assess the incorrect limb (left vs. right) or the incorrect movement, as these are considered critical clinical errors. learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13
learning_activities.topic: Professional communcation Professional Communication is a 2-hour, in-person, theory-driven tutorial held on Wednesdays from 8am to 10am during weeks 1–13 as part of the OCTY7808 course. Students enrolled in OCTY7811 are required to attend the professional communication stream within OCTY7808. These tutorials are not recorded and are designed as interactive, experiential learning sessions. They focus on developing the professional communication skills and professionalism required for effective therapeutic communication and success as an occupational therapist. Students are expected to attend all sessions, participate actively, and engage in both individual and peer-based reflection. The tutorials provide opportunities for small-group practice and refinement of specific communication skills. A detailed schedule of tutorial topics will be available on Learn.UQ.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 5 To Week 12
learning_activities.topic: Functional Anatomy Practicals The Functional Anatomy Module consists of 3-hour, in-person practical sessions held on Thursdays from 8 am to 11 am during weeks 5–12. These practicals are not recorded and are designed as hands-on, experiential learning sessions. They focus on developing students’ understanding of functional anatomy through active exploration, application, and skill development. Students are expected to attend all sessions, participate actively, and engage in practical activities to support their learning. The sessions provide opportunities for students to apply anatomical knowledge in a functional context, working both individually and collaboratively. Emphasis is placed on linking anatomical structures to movement, function, and occupational performance while learning ROM/MMT assessment skills. Further details, including a schedule of practical topics, will be available on Learn.UQ.
